               <ns0:head>CHAP. V.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>AFter this <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 23.2. Deut. 16.1.</ns0:note> there was a feast of the Jews <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Tho there be some that think the Feast mentioned here was that of <ns0:hi>Pentecost,</ns0:hi> and others, that it was the <ns0:hi>Feast of Tabernacles,</ns0:hi> yet the most and best Interpreters judge it was the Feast of the <ns0:hi>Passeover</ns0:hi> that is here mentioned. And that this was the second <ns0:hi>Passeover</ns0:hi> which happened after our Saviour had entred upon his Publick Ministry. We read of the first, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.13. and from that Verse of that Chap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, to this Chapter, the Evangelist (as they think) hath been relating so much of our Saviours Actions, until the Second Passeover, as it was the Will of God we should have upon Publick Authentick Record, and had not been Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />corded by the other Evangelists, who give a further account of his Actions done this Year, <ns0:hi>Mat. Ch.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9. <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 1. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 5. In the time of our Saviours Publick Ministry (which was three Years and a half) there were four Passeovers. The other Evangelists take notice but of one of them, and that the last. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> is thought to have mentioned all the four; the first, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.13. the second in this place, the third, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.4. the fourth, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.1. Another Reason they give why the Feast of the Passeover should be here intended, is, because from about that time to the Harvest were four Months, according to what our Saviour had said, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 4.35.</ns0:note>: and Jesus went up to Hierusalem <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Jesus went up to the Passeover, to <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> to shew his Obedience to his Fathers Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 16.16.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 Now there is at Hierusalem by the sheep <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>market</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">We read in Scripture of <ns0:hi>Sheep-gate</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Hierusalem, Neh.</ns0:hi> 3.1. There was also a Market for Sheep, and other Cattel, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 14.26. Some therefore add <ns0:hi>Market,</ns0:hi> others add <ns0:hi>Gate</ns0:hi> to the word in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> signifying Sheep:</ns0:note> a pool <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Near to this <ns0:hi>Gate</ns0:hi> or Market, there was a Pool, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, some Translate it a Fish-pool, others (more properly) a place to wash, or to Swim in (the word deriveth from a Verb that signifies to Swim.) They say, there were two such Pools within the compass of the Mount on which the Temple stood, the one Eastward, called the <ns0:hi>upper Pool,</ns0:hi> 2 Kings 18.17. The other Westward, near to the Sheep-gate. The one was called <ns0:hi>Bethesda,</ns0:hi> the other, the <ns0:hi>Pool of Siloam,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>the Kings Garden,</ns0:hi> Nehem. 3.15. mentioned also by our Evangelist, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.7. They say, the Waters of these Pools were supplied from a Fountain called <ns0:hi>Siloam</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which was not always full of water, but the water bubled up in it at certain times with a great noise, coming (as was thought) through hollow places of the Earth, and Quarries of hard stones. These Waters of <ns0:hi>Shiloah</ns0:hi> are mentioned, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.6. and said <ns0:hi>to go soft<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y</ns0:hi>; from <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> place, these Waters are concluded a <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the <ns0:hi>Kingd<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>m of David, and of Christ.</ns0:hi> This being admitted, it is not to be wondred that they had that Healing Vertue given unto them (as some judge) just about the coming of Christ; for it should appear by <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.7. that the <ns0:hi>Pool of Siloam, as</ns0:hi> well as that of <ns0:hi>Bethesda</ns0:hi> had so; for in former times it is thought to have been of use chiefly to wash Garments in, and Sacrifices when they were slain. Some wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l have them to have derived their Healing Vertue from thence, but that is vain, their Healing Vertue was doubtless derived from the Lord that healeth us.</ns0:note>, which is called in the He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brew tongue Bethesda <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This Pool in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> was called <ns0:hi>Bethesda,</ns0:hi> which some Interpret, <ns0:hi>The House of pour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing out,</ns0:hi> because as some fancy, the Blood of the Sacrifices was there poured out (but that is a great mistake, for that was to be poured out at the Altar) or because <ns0:hi>Rain-water</ns0:hi> (as some think) was poured into it; or (which is more probable) because waters were poured into it out of the Conduit mentioned 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 20.20. But others Interpret it, <ns0:hi>The house of Grace, Mercy,</ns0:hi> &c. because of Gods great goodness shewed the People, in giving this Healing Vertue to these Waters.</ns0:note>, having five porches <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The five <ns0:hi>Porches</ns0:hi> belonging to this <ns0:hi>Pool</ns0:hi> seem to have been five Apartments for Impotent men t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> walk in, or rest themselves in, when they came to wash themselves in the Pool.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 In these <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">In these <ns0:hi>Apartments</ns0:hi> (called here Porches) there were a great number of Sick Persons, some labouring under one Infirmity, some under another: Some blind, some lame, waiting for the time when</ns0:note> lay a great multitude of impotent folk, of blind, halt, withered, waiting for the mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving of the water <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">the water should be troubled.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 For an Angel went down at a certain season into the Pool, and troubled the water <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This water had not always in it this Healing Vertue, but <ns0:hi>onely when it was troubled,</ns0:hi> and this was at a <ns0:hi>certain season,</ns0:hi> how often, the Scripture hath not determined (some will have it to be onely at their great Feasts, of the <ns0:hi>Passe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />over,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pentecost,</ns0:hi> &c. but the S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ripture saith no such thing.) None must think that the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> appeared in any visible shape, but the roiling or troubling of the water was a certain sign, that that was the time when alone they were Medicinal</ns0:note>: whoso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ever first after the troubling of the water, stepped in, was made whole of whatsoever Disease he had <ns0:note n="k," place="bottom">nor were many healed at one time, but onely one Person, that could first get into this water, he was Healed, let his Disease be what it would. The waters not being constantly Medicinal, but at a certain time, when they were ro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>led; and then, 2. not for all, but onely to h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>m who could first get in. And 3. for any Disease, of what sort, or kind soever his Disease was, sufficiently confuteth the Opinion of those who fancy that the Waters derived this Healing Vertue from the Entrails of the Beasts Offered in Sacrifice, being washed there, for besides that this is de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nied by some, who say, those Entrails were washed in a Room on purpose for that use within the Temple; if they had derived their Healing Vertue from thence in a Natural Rational way, they would have exerted their Vertue upon more than him who first stepped in, and that not at the time onely when they were roiled, nor would their Vertue have extended to all kind of Diseases. Of what ever use this Pool therefore was before, certain it is at this time God made use of the Water in it to heal, and so as men might see that it healed not by any Natural, but a Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />culous Operation. The Scriptures of the O d Testament make no mention of it. And it is observed by those who are ve<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sed in the <ns0:hi>Iewish Rabbins,</ns0:hi> that neither do they make the least mention of it: Which makes it very probable, that they had this Vertue, not from the time of the build<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the Sheep-gate by <ns0:hi>Shallum,</ns0:hi> Nehem. 3.15. Nor from the time when the <ns0:hi>Asmon<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>an</ns0:hi> Family was extinct; or the rebui<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ding, or further building and adorning the Temple by <ns0:hi>Herod,</ns0:hi> but a little before the <ns0:hi>Birth of Christ,</ns0:hi> as a Figure of him being now coming, who, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 13.1. was a <ns0:hi>Fountain</ns0:hi> opened for <ns0:hi>the House of David, and the Inha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bitants of Hierusalem</ns0:hi>; and from whom is both our <ns0:hi>clean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing,</ns0:hi> and our <ns0:hi>healing,</ns0:hi> as these Waters, which before had a cleansing, and now received also an healing Vertue.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:338" />5 And a certain man was there which had an infirmity thirty and eight years <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">What this mans Name was, or what his Circumstan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces in the World, or what his particular Disease was, we are not told; nor is it said that he had lyen there thirty eight years, but that he had so long laboured under his Weakness; which whether it was the Palsie or no, is un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />certain; probably it was a Disease hardly curable by Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane Art, and ordinary means; for it cannot be thought but in that time he had used all rational means, which he finding of no value as to his case, he came and lay at this Fountain, waiting for a Cure in this way of Miraculous Operation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 VVhen Jesus saw him lye, and knew that he had been now a long time <ns0:hi>in that case</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Christ as God, knew the particular time when this Infirmity seized him, which was eight years or upward be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore our Saviours Birth, and about the time when the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> was re-edified, or rather enlarged and further adorned by <ns0:hi>Herod.</ns0:hi> As Man, he pitieth his Case</ns0:note>, he saith unto him, VVilt thou be made whole <ns0:note n="n;" place="bottom">he ask<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth him, if he was willing to be made whole? Not that he doubted of his willingness; for what Sick man was ever unwilling to be healed? Besides that, he knew that the poor man lay there for that very purpose; but that he might make him declare his miserable, helpless state and condition, and draw out his Faith, and Hope in himself; and from his Answer, take an occasion to heal him, and make the Spectators more attentive to his Miracle.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 The impotent man <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">What his particular Impotency was, the Scripture doth not tell us: Some have (not improbably) judged it the <ns0:hi>Palsie,</ns0:hi> which depriveth the Person of <ns0:hi>Motion,</ns0:hi> by the stoppage of the Animal Spirits, so that without help he cannot move from one place to another, which it is ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifest this poor man could not; for</ns0:note> answered, (Sir) I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the Pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">he complaineth for want of help, that he could not get into the Pool.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Jesus saith unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 9.6. Mark 2.11. Luke 5.24.</ns0:note> Rise, take up thy bed, and walk <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Our Lord will let this poor man know, that the Wa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters, and the Angel, derived their Power from him; and that he with a word could do as much for him, as the Waters ro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>led by the Angel could effect: He therefore bids him <ns0:hi>Arise, and take up his bed, and walk,</ns0:hi> that others might see, and be assured that he was perfectly Cured.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And immed<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ately the man was made whole <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The mans strength returneth immediately; he</ns0:note>, and took up his bed, and walked <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">is able immediately to <ns0:hi>arise, take up his Bed,</ns0:hi> and to <ns0:hi>walk.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.14.</ns0:note> on the same day was the Sabbath <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">All this was done on the Sabbath-day; on which day it was unlawful to carry any Burthens, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 17.21.24. And by the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Canons it was punishable by Death, or Scourging. But our Saviour had a mind to let the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> know that he was Lord of the Sabbath, and what had been unlawful without his special Command, became Lawful by it. Neither was this against the sense of the Law, tho against the letter of it; the Law onely prohibited Civil La<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour, and carrying Burdens for their own profit, and in the way of their Trade; it forbad the doing of nothing which was to be done as a publick Testimony of the Goodness and Mercy of God shewed to Persons; and by this our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour opens a way for his Correction of their Erroneous Opinions about the true Sanctification of the Sabbath: We shall observe, that our Saviour used the like Phrase to him that had the Palsie, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.4. and to the Centurions Daughter, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 5 41. <ns0:hi>Damsel, Arise</ns0:hi>: And to <ns0:hi>Lazarus, Ch</ns0:hi> 11.43. <ns0:hi>Lazarus, come forth</ns0:hi>; which our Saviour did for the testification of the Miracle to all that should see them. It is further observed by <ns0:hi>Heinsins,</ns0:hi> that our Saviour did many Miracles on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath-day,</ns0:hi> because that day was the usual time when the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were wont to Consult the Prophets for help, as may be learned from 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 4.23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 The Jews therefore said unto him that was cured, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 20.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Neh. 13.19. Jer. 17.22. & Mat. 12.2. Mark 2.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Luke 6.2.</ns0:note> It is the Sabbath-day: it is not lawful for thee to carry <ns0:hi>thy</ns0:hi> bed <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">That is, according to the letter of the Law, they un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood not that Christ was the Lord of the Sabbath; their Cavil argued their want both of <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in Christ, and Charity also toward their Neighbour.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 He answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up thy bed and walk <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He makes them as good an Answer as could well be imagined; the sum of which was, he believed that he that had thus Healed him, was a Prophet, and so did what he did by a Divine Authority, which it was Lawful for him to Obey, contrary to their Traditions; tho who this particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lar Person was, or what his Name was, were things as yet not known to him (as we shall by and by read) yet he seemeth sensible that he was Healed by a Power more than Humane.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Then asked they him, What man is that which said unto thee, Take up thy bed and walk <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Impotent man that was Healed, seemed to op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose the Authority of God (by vertue of which he be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved himself healed) to the Authority of Man, which made it unlawful for him on the Sabbath-day to take up his bed and walk. The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> taking no notice of Christs be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing God, or so much as a Prophet sent from God, do not ask, <ns0:hi>Who was he,</ns0:hi> but, <ns0:hi>What man was he that said,</ns0:hi> &c. Opposing the Command of God, to the Command of Man. It is as much as if they had said, The Law of God hath Commanded that no Burdens should be carried on the Sab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bath-day: Now, what is <ns0:hi>that man</ns0:hi> that dare teach thee or any one to do what is contrary to the Law of God?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And he that was healed, wist not who he was <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Christ came as a stranger to the Pool, and onely wrought this Miracle, so as the Impotent man that was Healed had no time to enquire who he was</ns0:note>: For Jesus had conveyed himself away, a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>from the multitude that was.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> multitude being in <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> place <ns0:note n="z;" place="bottom">and there being there a croud of People, Christ had through the People conveyed himself away; so as the man could not find him to shew them the man who had so said unto him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Afterward Jesus findeth him in the Temple <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Walking in the outward Court of the Temple, or some part of it, where People ordinarily Walked;</ns0:note>, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 12.45. Chap. 8.11.</ns0:note> sin no more, lest a worst thing come unto thee <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">he chargeth him to sin no more, lest a worse thing betided him; hereby letting him and us know, that sin is the usual cause of Diseases, and an Holy walking the best Preserva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive of Health; and that God hath further Revelations of his wrath against sin and sinners, than what do, or can be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fall them in this Life.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 The man departed, and told the Jews that it was Jesus which had made him whole <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">It were very uncharitable to judge, that this poor man went to the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Magistrates, to inform against Christ, who had been so kind to him; and much more probable that he went in the simplicity of his Heart, desirous both to publish what Christ had done to his Honour; and also to do good to others, who might also stand in need of his help.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the Sabbath-day <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">But the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> made another use of it; seeking from hence an advantage against him, because he had <ns0:hi>violated the Sabbath,</ns0:hi> which they often made a Capital Crime.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 But Jesus answered them <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">We read of no Objection they made to Christ, as to what he had done, onely that <ns0:hi>they Persecuted him,</ns0:hi> which they might do without speaking to him: But it should seem by what we read in this Verse, that some of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had Objected to him, his <ns0:hi>violation of the Sabbath</ns0:hi> (as they thought) yet, as we before noted, <ns0:hi>Answering</ns0:hi> (in the Dia<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lect of the Gospel) doth often signifie no more than the beginning of a Discourse upon some proper occasion of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fered.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14.10.</ns0:note> My Father worketh hitherto, and I work <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Our Saviour defendeth himself, from the Example of his Father, in the remembrance of whose resting from his work of Creation on the Seventh day from the begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning of the Creation, the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> kept their <ns0:hi>Sabbath</ns0:hi>; who tho he rested from his work of Creation, yet hitherto worketh, as well on the Sabbath-day as any other day, by his preservation of Created Beings: So (saith he) I who am the Son of this Father, also work; upholding all things by the word of my Power, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 1.3. So that works of Divine Providence are Lawful on the Sabbath-day, such was this. I work no other way than my Father still <ns0:hi>worketh,</ns0:hi> tho he rested on the Seventh day from the Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:338" />18 Therefore the Jews <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.19.</ns0:note> sought the more to kill him, because he not onely had broken the Sabbath <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This yet enraged the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> more: They had before against him a Charge of breaking the Sabbath, or at least, teaching another to break it, (in their Opinion)</ns0:note>, but said also, That God was his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.33.</ns0:note> making himself equal with God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">but now he had (as they judged) spoken Blasphemy, calling God <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi>; not in the sense the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> so called him, and all good Christians are Licensed to call him; but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, his proper Father, or his own Father; by which (as they truly said) he made himself <ns0:hi>equal with God.</ns0:hi> Nor did he by that alone, make himself equal with God, but he ascribed also to himself a co-operation with God, in works proper to God alone: Nor did he think this any Robbery, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.6. This was their Charge; we shall now hear how our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our defendeth himself against it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Then answered Jesus, and said unto them, Verily, Verily, I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 30. Chap. 8.38. and 9.4.</ns0:note> The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther do <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Consider Christ as God; so, he can do nothing but what the Father doth; that is, nothing that respected Created Beings: For it is a known Rule, <ns0:hi>That the works of the Trinity out of it self are not divided</ns0:hi>; whatsoever one Person doth, the others do; tho to denote the order of the Trinities working, some works are most ordinarily ascri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bed to the Father (such are the works of <ns0:hi>Creation</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Providence.</ns0:hi>) Some to the Son, as <ns0:hi>Redemption</ns0:hi>; some to the Holy Spirit, as <ns0:hi>Sanctification</ns0:hi>; yet they are not so as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cribed to any Person, but that other Scriptures justifie the co-operation of all three Persons. Consider the Son as the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>; so also it is true, That the Son <ns0:hi>can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.</ns0:hi> Nor is this any diminution to the Glory of Christ, nor doth it speak any Impotency in him; from whence the <ns0:hi>Arrians</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cinians</ns0:hi> would conclude his Inferiority to his Father; but rather his <ns0:hi>Perfection,</ns0:hi> that he did onely what pleased the Father: So that Phrase [<ns0:hi>What he seeth the Father do</ns0:hi>] is to be Interpreted. And that term [<ns0:hi>can do nothing</ns0:hi>] signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies no more than, he <ns0:hi>doth,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>will do nothing.</ns0:hi> See such an usage of the Phrase, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 19.22. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 16.2. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.39. From this he leaveth them easily to conclude, that what he had done, in Curing this Impotent Man upon the <ns0:hi>Sab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bath-day,</ns0:hi> was the <ns0:hi>Fathers work,</ns0:hi> tho by him. For what<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever the Father doth, or willeth, the same doth the Son likewise. From hence will appear an easie Solution to the difficulty arising upon the first view of the words, <ns0:hi>viz. How these words can prove Christ equal with the Father, when they rather prove the contrary</ns0:hi>; because he <ns0:hi>can do no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doth.</ns0:hi> Some seek a Solution in the words <ns0:hi>cannot</ns0:hi>; he that cannot do those things which God cannot do, is equal with God. Some seek it in the word <ns0:hi>see</ns0:hi>; which they say, signifieth here an identity of Nature and Will. Some seek the So<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lution in the word <ns0:hi>do,</ns0:hi> which, they say, signifieth <ns0:hi>to will</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>consent to.</ns0:hi> The best Solution is to be taken from those words [<ns0:hi>of himself</ns0:hi>] the Son hath done many things which he did not see the Father do, but he did them not <ns0:hi>of him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self.</ns0:hi> Our Saviours meaning is plainly this: The Son nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther willeth, nor can do any thing, but what the Father willeth, and doth in him: Therefore he is one in Essence with the Father, and equal to him.</ns0:note>, For whatsoever things he doth, these also doth the Son likewise <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The Son doth those things which the Father doth; and as the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> he doth those things which the Father willeth to be done.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.35.</ns0:note> the Father loveth the son <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Both as his Son by Eternal Generation, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 3.17. and also as the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> sent by him into the World, to fi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nish the work the Father had given him to do: And</ns0:note>, and shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth him all things that himself doth, <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">look as <ns0:hi>a Father</ns0:hi> will make his Son acquainted with all that he doth; and not onely so, but communicates all his <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> and Skill to his Son, so far as he can: So the Father com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />municateth all his Power to the Son, working all things in him, and by him; and he will in and by him work greater things than this, healing this poor man; he will by him raise the dead, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> and he will shew him greater works than these, that you may marvel <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That you may marvel; Christ knew, that they would not believe, and all the effect that his Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racles had upon the generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> was but causing in them a stupefaction, amazement, and admiration, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.47. whereas it was their Duty, not onely to <ns0:hi>marvel,</ns0:hi> but to have believed also; without which their Admiration did but cause that they had no Cloak for their sin.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickneth <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">He seemeth not to speak of what God will do in the general Resurrection, but of those whom the Lord raised up from the dead in the Old Testament, by <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elisha.</ns0:hi> The giving of, and restoring unto Life, are things proper unto God, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.39. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2.6.</ns0:note>, even so the son quickneth whom he will <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">So the Son <ns0:hi>quickneth whom he will.</ns0:hi> God hath given unto me a Power to raise from the dead whom I will (as he did raise up <ns0:hi>Iairus</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Daughter, Mat.</ns0:hi> 9.25. and the Widows Son, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 7.14. and <ns0:hi>Lazarus, Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.43. This was one of those greater works, of which our Saviour spake in the former Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 For the father judgeth no man <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Alone he judgeth no man, he judgeth no man but by the Son, no man without the Son, but</ns0:note>, but hath <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 11.27<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and 28.18. Chap. 3.35<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and 17.2.</ns0:note> committed all Judgment unto the son <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">committed all Judgment in the administration of the Mediatory Kingdom in the Church to his Son, and by his Son will Judge the World at the last day.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 That all men should honour the Son <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">That his Son might be Honoured by all men, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 2.11, 12. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.10.</ns0:note>, even as they honour the Father <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">with the same Honour which is given to the Father;</ns0:note>. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 2.23.</ns0:note> He that honoureth not the son, honoureth not the father which hath sent him <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">for the Son is sent by the Father, not as one Inferior to him, as a Servant is sent by his Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster; but as an Equal is sent by his Friend, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 4.34. and 6.38. and 7.28. And look, as a great Prince, when he sendeth his Embassador, expecteth that those to whom he is sent, should give him Honour, and the same Honour as to himself; so doth the Father: So that he that Honoureth not the Son, Honoureth not the Father which sent him. It is a Text which reflecteth dreadfully upon such as Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour not Christ, especially the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Socinians,</ns0:hi> who professedly do not Honour him with the same Honour with which they yet pretend to Honour the Father; and are con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluded by this Text not in truth to Honour the Father.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Verily, Verily, I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.18. and 6.40. and 8.51.</ns0:note> He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">He that so heareth my words, that they are not a mere sound in his Ears, nor affect his Heart with some mere sud<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den and vanishing Passion; but so, that he gives an assent to them upon my Authority, and that firmly and steadily believeth him that sent me (the Particle <ns0:hi>on</ns0:hi> seemeth not well put in by our Translators; in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>) giveth Credit to the words of my Father that sent me, believing that I am his onely begotten Son, whom he hath sent into the World, and receiving me as such, <ns0:hi>hearing me</ns0:hi> according to the Command of the Voice from Heaven, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 17.5.</ns0:note>, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">he hath a certain Title to Everlasting Life; and hath received the first fruits of that Harvest, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.23. the incorruptible Seed of the Word, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.23. and already sitteth in Heavenly places in Christ Jesus, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.6. and <ns0:hi>hath the Kingdom of God within him,</ns0:hi> Luke 17.21. and shall not come into that Judgment which shall issue in Eternal Condemnation</ns0:note>, but is passed from death to life <ns0:note n="y;" place="bottom">but is passed out of a state of Spiritual Death, into a state of Spiritual Life; and shall be at last eternally saved, and pass into the actual frui<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion and enjoyment of Life Eternal.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Verily, Verily, I say unto you, the hour is coming, and now is, when <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 2.5.</ns0:note> the dead shall hear the voice of the son of God <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Some understand this concerning the special Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection of such Bodies as Christ raised while he was upon the Earth from Death to Life (of which number was <ns0:hi>La<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zarus</ns0:hi> and the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Iairus,</ns0:hi> &c.) Others understand it of the general Resurrection, spoken of, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29. That which favoureth this sense is, because here is no mention of believing, but onely hearing a voice. But the most and best Interpreters rather understand these words of those who are dead in Trespasses and Sins; and the quickning and Life mentioned, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.1. which is called <ns0:hi>the first Resurrection, Rev.</ns0:hi> 20.5. because of what was said immediately before, that such a one <ns0:hi>is passed from death to life</ns0:hi>; and what was said before, <ns0:hi>He that heareth my word,</ns0:hi> agreeth with what is said here, <ns0:hi>of hearing the voice of Christ</ns0:hi>; and what fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />loweth, seemeth better to agree with this sense. And <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29. speak plainly of the Second and General Resurrection of the Body.</ns0:note>, and they that hear shall live <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Those who so hear the Voice of Christ in the Gospel, as to give a firm and steady assent to it; and upon the Credit of it, shall receive Christ as their Mediator and Saviour, shall live Eternally; they do live the life of Grace, and shall live the life of Glory.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:339" />26 For as the Father hath life in himself, so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">How the Eternal Father hath Life in himself, is ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vious to every Capacity; for he is the first mover, and therefore must have his Life in, and from himself, and not from any other: And he is the <ns0:hi>first cause,</ns0:hi> and therefore that Life which floweth from him to all Created Beings, must first be in him, as in its Fountain. But in what sense it is said, that he hath <ns0:hi>given to the Son to have life in him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self</ns0:hi>; whether as God, by his Eternal Generation, or as the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and Mediator betwixt God and Man; and so the Fountain of <ns0:hi>Spiritual Life</ns0:hi> to Believers is more que<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stioned. Those who understand it, as to the Divine Nature, say, that this Phrase [<ns0:hi>hath life in himself</ns0:hi>] is expressive of the name <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi>; and that Christ is proved to be the true <ns0:hi>Iehovah,</ns0:hi> by what is here said, <ns0:hi>that he hath life in himself.</ns0:hi> But they distinguish betwixt having life from, or by himself, and <ns0:hi>having life in himself.</ns0:hi> The Text saith, It is given to Christ to have Life in himself. But there are other Interpreters, who seem better to understand it of <ns0:hi>Christ as Mediator,</ns0:hi> to whom it is given to have <ns0:hi>Life in himself,</ns0:hi> to communicate to his Creatures; and think it is well Interpreted by <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.4. <ns0:hi>In him was life, and the life was the light of men.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And hath given him authority to execute judgment also <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To have the power of Life and Death, the Keys of both; to Rule and Govern the World, and to Judge it at the last day.</ns0:note>, because he is the Son of man <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 17.31. <ns0:hi>He hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness, by that man whom he hath ordained,</ns0:hi> &c. So <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.8. <ns0:hi>Being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross: wherefore God hath also highly exalted him,</ns0:hi> &c. Some think that the sense is, because he was that Son of Man, who was the <ns0:hi>Seed of the woman</ns0:hi> promised, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.15. The Son of Man Prophecied of by <ns0:hi>Daniel, Chap.</ns0:hi> 7.13, 14. And that the term, <ns0:hi>Son of man</ns0:hi> (here) signifieth his Office as <ns0:hi>Media<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tor.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Marvel not at this; for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Do not marvel at this Power which I tell you the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther hath given me, to execute in the World Justice and Judgment; to raise some particular Persons from a Natu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Death, and whom he pleaseth from the Spiritual death of sin: For the hour is coming, when all those who are in the Graves, shall by an <ns0:hi>Arch-Angel, Mat.</ns0:hi> 24.31. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 4.16. hear my Voice, commanding them to Arise; and they shall obey my command.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 25.32, 33, 46. 1 Thes. 4.16.</ns0:note> shal<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">And come forth; not all to be made partakers of Eternal Life and Glory. There shall be a Resurrection un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Life, which onely they shall obtain, <ns0:hi>who have done good, walking in the Commandments of God</ns0:hi>; not because they have done good, as if their goodness had Merited any such thing; for Eternal Life is the gift of God, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6.23. But others who</ns0:note> and they that have done evil <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">have wrought Iniquity, and died with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out Repentance and Faith in me, shall rise</ns0:note>, unto the resurrection of damnation <ns0:note n="h," place="bottom">that the Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stice of God may by me, the Judge of the Quick and the Dead, be executed upon them unto Eternal Condemnation. This <ns0:hi>Daniel, Chap.</ns0:hi> 12.2 calleth <ns0:hi>shame, and everlasting contempt.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 25.46. calls it <ns0:hi>Everlasting Punishment.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 I can of my own self do nothing <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Neither considered as God, or as Mediator. As God the Father and Christ were one, and what one Person in the Holy Trinity doth, all do: so that he did nothing in that capacity separately from his Father. As Mediator, he did nothing of his self; he finished the work which his Father gave him to do.</ns0:note>: as I hear, I judge; and my judgment is just <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">As the Father revealed his Will to him for the administration of his Mediatory Kingdom in the World, so he Judged: And therefore his Judgment must necessarily be just and true</ns0:note>, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause I <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.38.</ns0:note> seek not my own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me <ns0:note n="l;" place="bottom">for his Will was not a Will proper to himself, so as it was not also common to his Father, but divers from the Will of his Father; but as his Essence, so his Will was the same with his Father; and he being by the Father sent into the World to do his Will, accordingly did nothing as Mediator but what was his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers Will as well as his own; in nothing divers from his Fathers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 5.14.</ns0:note> If I bear witness of my self, my witness is not true <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This seemeth to contradict what he saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.14. <ns0:hi>Tho I bear record of my self, yet my record is true</ns0:hi>: But our Saviour here speaketh according to the common Opinion of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> or indeed of men, who are ready to suspect any ones Testimony, who testifieth of himself: He tells them, he could grant them this, tho his Record of himself was true, yet he could allow them their common received Opinion, and saying, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.13. That the Testimony of one testifying of himself, is suspicious; for it is certain that a man may testifie truth of himself, onely such a te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony is suspicious; he tells them, he did not onely testifie of himself, his Reputation did not stand upon his own single word.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 17.5.</ns0:note> There is another that beareth witness of me <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The Father by a voice from Heaven testified of Christ, that he was his well-beloved Son, in whom he was well pleased, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 3.17. Some understand it of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> of whom he speaketh, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. But he naming <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> in the next verse, it seems most proper to understand this of the Father testifying of Christ, both at his Baptism, and also at his Transfiguration<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and to Interpret the next Verse, as speaking of another Testimony distinct from that of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and I know<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that the witness which he wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesseth of me is true <ns0:note n="o:" place="bottom">And (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>I know</ns0:hi>; that is, I am fully assured that his Testimony of me is true; for God is that God who cannot lye, but is truth it self. So that I do not barely testifie of my self; for my Father, whom you all own to be a God of truth, and who cannot lye, and whom I know to be such, he testifieth of me, and none can contradict his Testimony.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.7, 15, 19, 27.</ns0:note> Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Ye sent Priests and <ns0:hi>Levites</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Iohn, Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.29. He was a man of Reputation among you, for all the People judged him a Prophet; and he had an In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terest in <ns0:hi>Herods</ns0:hi> Court: He bare witness (he doth not say to me, but) to the Truth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 But I receive not testimony from man <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That is, not for my own sake; for otherwise he did receive testimony from man, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 15.27. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.8. That must be Truth, to which any one can give a true Testimony. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> by his Testimony added nothing to me. I was what I am, before <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> testified concerning me</ns0:note>: but these things I say, that ye might be sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved <ns0:note n="r." place="bottom">I onely spake of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s testimony for your sake, that you might believe, and be saved.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 He was a burning and a shining light <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">I do not speak this to lessen <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> in any of your thoughts; he was a Famous Light, burning in the knowledge and love of the Truth; shining both in his Doctrine, in pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lishing the Truth, and also in Holiness of Life and Conver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sation: He was not <ns0:hi>that light, Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.8. but he was a Light, not <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 5.14. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 8.16.</ns0:note>, and ye were willing for a season to rejoyce in his light <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">And you for a small time pretended a great Affection for <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and came with great Zeal to hear him, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 3.5. and 21.26. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 1.5. hoping that he was the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> or at least <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> or that <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> in him re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vived again: But when they saw that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> did only bear Record to Christ, they grew cold in their Affection, not liking either his Doctrine, or the strictness of his Life, or the tidings that he brought; looking for a far more splen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />did and Glorious <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> than Christ appeared to them to be.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 5.9.</ns0:note> I have greater witness than <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> of John, <ns0:note n="⸫" place="bottom">Not than that of my <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31, 32. but than that of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> (last mentioned;) nor doth he say a <ns0:hi>truer,</ns0:hi> but a <ns0:hi>greater witness.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> for the works which the Father hath given me to finish <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The works which his Father sent him to do, his fulfilling of the Law, his publication of the Gospel, the Miracles which he wrought, were all of them works which his Father had given him to finish. Christ often appealeth to the works which he had done, as sufficiently testifying of him, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.25. 37, 38. and 14.10, 11. and 15.24. And it is plain, that the People lookt upon them as a great testimony, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 3.2. and 9.32, 33. The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> avoided the force of th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s testimony impudently, some of them saying, that he did them by the help of the Devil, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 12.24. Others pretending (more lately) that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was to work no Miracles; but that is expresly contrary to what we have, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.31. and is doubtless a device of later years.</ns0:note>, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">But it is a greater Question, how the Miracles of Christ bear witness of him; and whether they were onely a probable, or a certain and infallible Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony of his Deity. Those that think them an infallible Testimony, say, 1. <ns0:hi>That he did works which none else did,</ns0:hi> John 15.24. 2. That he did them by his own Power, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 6.19. <ns0:hi>There went Vertue out of him, and healed them all.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>That they were done in confirmation of the Doctrine to that purpose, which he Preached,</ns0:hi> which God would not have confirmed by Miracles, had not he been sent of God to work such things. Those that think they were not a certain and infallible Testimony, say, 1. <ns0:hi>That the Prophets and Apostles</ns0:hi> also wrought Miracles. 2. <ns0:hi>That our Saviour tells his Apostles, they should do greater works than he had done.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>That the doing of them from his own Power, was a thing could not be known to others</ns0:hi>; so could be no Testimony to them. But our Saviour did not onely himself raise the dead, cast out Devils, and work other Miracles; but he gave others also a Power to do it, which argued an Original Power in himself, and is more than we read of any Prophets or Apostles; who, tho they wrought such Miraculous Operations, yet having not that Power Originally in, and from themselves, could not communi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cate it to others.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:339" />37 And the Father himself which hath sent me, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 3.17. Chap. 8.18.</ns0:note> hath born witness of me <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Not onely in my <ns0:hi>Baptism,</ns0:hi> and at my <ns0:hi>Transfiguration</ns0:hi> by an audible Voice from Heaven, but by the Voice of his Prophets, by whom he spoke to your Fathers.</ns0:note>; Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 4.12.</ns0:note> nor seen his shape <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">You have no knowledge of kim, nor any acquaintance with him. It is expounded, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 38. <ns0:hi>Ye have not his word abiding in you</ns0:hi>: For tho indeed God appeared to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in no <ns0:hi>shape</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>similitude</ns0:hi>; yet they (that is, their Fore-fathers) had heard his Voice, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 4.12. speaking out of the midst of the fire, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33. God being an incorporeal Being, hath no such organs of Speech as we have, by which we declare our minds unto others; but God had formed an audible Voice, by which he revealed his will unto the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>: So as it could onely be said of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> of that Generation and their Forefathers, from the time of giving the Law, that they had not heard his Voice; for <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.19. they then desired that <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> might speak to them, and that God would speak no more immediately. Accordingly, he did <ns0:hi>by the Prophets</ns0:hi> speak to them, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 1.3. but they would not believe them; no, not when he spake to them by his Son, who knew his will.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And you have not his word abiding in you <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Though they had heard the word of the Lord, their Forefathers, <ns0:hi>by the Prophets,</ns0:hi> and in that Generation by <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist</ns0:hi> (the Messenger sent before Christs face) and now by Christ himself, whom the Father had sent; yet the word of the Lord had no place in their Hearts, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.37. it was unto them as a Tale told; they received the sound of it, but it was not graven in their Hearts.</ns0:note>, for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">And this appeared, because as of themselves they had no inti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />macy of Communion with God to know his mind: So when the Son was sent out of the Bosom of the Father to reveal God unto them, yet they would not receive him, so as to give any steady, fixed assent to what he revealed, and to yield him any just and true Obedience.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 8.20. and 34.16. Luke 16.29. Acts 17.11.</ns0:note> Search the Scriptures <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The words may be read either <ns0:hi>Imperatively</ns0:hi> (as our Translation readeth them) or <ns0:hi>Indicatively</ns0:hi>; you do search the Scriptures (that is, of the Old Testament, for the Books of the New Testament were not at that time writ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten) but as they had the Books of the Old Testament, so they made use of them: <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> was read in the Syna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gogues every <ns0:hi>Sabbath-day</ns0:hi>; and they (the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially) were very well versed both in the Law and the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets:</ns0:note>, for in them ye think ye have eternal life <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">They did agree that the way of Salvation and Everlasting Life was revealed unto them in the Holy Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures; nay, they did judge, that Eternal Life was to be obtained by their observation of the Law</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 18.15, 18. Luke 24.27. Chap. 1.45.</ns0:note> they are they which testifie of me <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They (saith our Saviour) are my principal Testimony; he doth not onely say, they testifie, but <ns0:hi>they are they that testifie.</ns0:hi> No Writings but those testifie of me; I principally appeal to them to give you an account of me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And ye will not come to me <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">You will not own, embrace, and receive me as the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and Saviour of the World, tho that be the onely means by which you can obtain</ns0:note>, that ye might have life <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">that Eternal Life which you pretend to be seeking after; and rightly think that the Scripture alone can shew you the way to. These two Verses teach us, 1. That the Holy Scriptures are the onely Writings which shew us the way to Life Eternal. 2. That not onely the Scriptures of the New, but also of the Old Testament, are of use in order thereunto, tho the Old Testament Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures shew us it more darkly, and those of the New Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stament shew it to us more clearly. 3. That both the one and the other point us to Christ, and to the receiving and embracing of him, as our Saviour, if we would have Life. 4. That it is not sufficient for us to search the Scriptures, to be versed in, and acquainted with them, unless we in Obedience to them come to Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 I receive not honour from men <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">I depend not upon the single Testimony of men: Or, I seek not, nor hunt after the Honour of men, nor regard what they think or say of me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">You pretend a great deal of Religion, and to do many things out of love to God, and a zeal for the Glory of God; but tho you can cheat others, yet you cannot de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive me; I that search the Heart, and try the Reins, and am a witness to your Actions, know that whatsoever you pretend, the true love of God dwelleth not in you; and that is the reason why you do not receive me.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 I am come in my Fathers name, and ye receive me not <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">I am come clothed with an Authority from my Father, sent by him for this very purpose, to reveal his will to men for their Salvation: I speak, I do nothing but by the Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority of my Father which sent me; nor do I aim at my own Glory, but the Glory of him that sent me; yet you give no Credit to my words, nor embrace me, as him whom God hath sent for the Saviour of Man.</ns0:note>: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Through the Corruption of your Hearts, and the just Judgment of God, <ns0:hi>giving you up to strong delusions to believe lyes,</ns0:hi> 2 Thes 2.11. If any Seducers come, without any Authority from God, never sent of him, nor speaking his words, nor seek<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing his Glory, or your good, you will readily enough receive them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 How can ye believe which receive honour from one another, and seek not <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 2.29.</ns0:note> the honour that <ns0:hi>cometh</ns0:hi> from God onely <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">It is evident that by <ns0:hi>receiving Honour from one another,</ns0:hi> is here to be understood the seeking and pursuing of Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour and Applause from men, without regard to the praise of God. So also <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.43. For otherwise it is Lawful for <ns0:hi>Parents</ns0:hi> to receive Honour from <ns0:hi>Children, Masters</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Servants, Princes,</ns0:hi> and other <ns0:hi>Magistrates,</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>People</ns0:hi>; but for men to be Ambitious of Honour and Applause of men, in neglect of the Honour and Praise of God, this is highly sinful; and it cannot be expected that any such Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons should so far deny themselves, and renounce their own works of Righteousness, as to accept of Christ and his Righteousness, and relye upon him alone for Life and Salvation. It is said, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.42, 43. <ns0:hi>That amongst the chief Rulers, many believed</ns0:hi>: Yet it is added, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43. <ns0:hi>For they loved the praise of men more then the praise of God.</ns0:hi> But those words, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43. seem rather to refer to the <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees,</ns0:hi> mentioned in the latter part of <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 42. where a Rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son is given, why tho many great Rulers <ns0:hi>believed,</ns0:hi> yet they did not <ns0:hi>confess Christ, because of the Pharisees.</ns0:hi> Or if those words, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43. be to be applyed to those of whom it is said, <ns0:hi>they believed, v.</ns0:hi> 42. we must distinguish concerning be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving, which in <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.42. signifieth no more than an assent given to him as a great Prophet, upon the Miracles they saw wrought by him: In this place, a true and lively Faith, receiving Christ as our Mediator and Saviour.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">There will be no need of my accusing you,</ns0:note>: there is <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> that accuseth you, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> Moses, in whom ye trust <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">you will need no other Accuser than that <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> for whom you have so great a Reverence, and for whose sake you contemn me, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.28, 29. They said, <ns0:hi>We are Moses his Disciples; we know that God spake unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is.</ns0:hi> This <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> (saith our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour) will accuse you unto the Father.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me, for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 12.3. and 18.18. and 22.18. and 49.10.</ns0:note> he wrote of me <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Had you given an hearty credit and understanding assent to <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>; that is, to the writings of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> for so the term is oft taken, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 16.31. and 24.27. you would have received me; as all the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> pointed to, and prefigured me, so he in particular wrote of me, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.15. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.15.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:340" />47 But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">But if you believe not his writings, who so plainly wrote of me, and whose writings you own, and have so great a Veneration for; how can I expect that you should believe the words of one whom you so vilifie and contemn? For tho my words be in themselves of greater Authority, yet I have not so much Credit with you as <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> had. But how doth our Saviour affirm, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 45. that they trusted in <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and deny here, that they did <ns0:hi>believe him? Answ.</ns0:hi> Some say, they believed with an <ns0:hi>implicite Faith</ns0:hi>; presuming upon the merits of <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac, Iacob</ns0:hi>; but not with an <ns0:hi>explicite Faith.</ns0:hi> Others say, they believed in the gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral, that whatsoever he wrote, was true; but they did not believe them in the true sense of them. <ns0:hi>Tarnovius</ns0:hi> thinks, That they trusted in <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> that they might be saved by their own works done in obedience to his Law; but they did not believe him, because they rejected him of whom <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> wrote, and to whom the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> was but a School-master. They refused him who was the <ns0:hi>Head of the corner,</ns0:hi> Psal. 118.22. Mat. 21.42.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
